### Observed differences

- In the later window, activity A01 appears in every trace (100% of 200 traces), whereas it was absent from all traces in the earlier window (0% of 200 traces). [OCC001]
- In the later window, activity A03 is always followed by A01 (100% of A03 occurrences), while in the earlier window A03 had no observed outgoing transition to A01. [DIR001]
- In the later window, A03 and A01 always co-occur, with A03 always occurring before A01; in the earlier window, traces contained only A03, with no A01. [REL001]
- The relative position of A03 shifted from the end of the trace (position 1.0) in the earlier window to a position just before A01 (about 0.86) in the later window, while A01 occupies the final position (1.0) in the later window. [POS001, POS002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the process changed by adding activity A01 as a new final step after A03, so that each case now executes A03 followed by A01, whereas before it executed only A03. This is directly shown by A01 appearing in all later traces, A03 always preceding A01, and A03 no longer being the last activity. The five control-flow items are far more than the 0.09 expected by chance, and they consistently describe the same structural change. A competing explanation that A01 existed but was simply unobserved before is unlikely given its complete absence in 200 earlier traces and its presence in all 200 later traces.
